stem: A 30-year-old woman with chronic diarrhea and weight loss has a duodenal biopsy showing complete loss of villi. Her malabsorption results mainly from loss of which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: A 600-fold amplification of absorptive surface area
options.misconception: None; folds, villi, and microvilli multiply the absorbing surface.
options.explanation: Circular folds, villi, and microvilli increase the small-intestinal mucosal surface area by 600-fold, with about 200 million microvilli per square millimeter; losing villi collapses this absorptive capacity.

options.label: B
options.text: The mucosal cells that secrete the hormone secretin
options.misconception: A hormone deficiency is being cast as the cause of generalized malabsorption.
options.explanation: Secretin regulates pancreatic bicarbonate release; its loss would impair acid neutralization, not the absorptive surface needed for nutrients.

options.label: C
options.text: Gut-associated lymphoid tissue within the mucosa
options.misconception: Immune tissue is being cast as an absorptive structure.
options.explanation: Mucosal lymphoid tissue defends against pathogens; it plays no direct role in absorbing nutrients from chyme.

options.label: D
options.text: The pacemaker cells that set the intestinal rhythm
options.misconception: A motility defect is being cast as the cause of the malabsorption.
options.explanation: Pacemaker activity drives segmentation and peristalsis; disordered motility alters transit but does not remove the surface area across which absorption occurs.

options.label: E
options.text: The colonic bacteria that synthesize key vitamins
options.misconception: Hindgut flora are being cast as the main site of nutrient uptake.
options.explanation: Colonic bacteria synthesize certain vitamins and ferment residue, but the bulk of nutrient absorption occurs across the small-intestinal villi.

context: Learning objective: structure serves absorption. Circular folds, villi, and microvilli multiply small-intestinal surface area 600-fold (~200 million microvilli/mm2); brush-border enzymes on the microvilli finish carbohydrate and protein digestion. Villous atrophy (as in celiac disease) therefore causes malabsorption and weight loss.
